summary: This is a Mol Labs public hypothesis card (P28) framing a research question about whether VIP (vasoactive intestinal peptide) retains neuroprotective or cognitive phenotype under conditions that abolish VPAC2-class attribution (via PG 99-465 antagonist or Vipr2 genetic LOF). The document is a structured research discussion proposing an assumption-kill experiment, cataloguing prior art (Brenneman, Gozes, Cunha-Reis, Harmar, Rangon, Shoge, Zaben), and noting that the key matched residual H2H experiment is currently EMPTY/UNKNOWN. No experimental data has been generated; the project is at TRL 1–2 (concept with literature-grounded rationale).

content_blocks.title: Hypothesis / Claim (P28)
content_blocks.content: On a matched rodent cognition/neuroprotection panel (Brenneman/Gozes-class or Rangon/Shoge-class style) ± VIP ± VPAC2 antagonist (PG 99-465 or VIP(6-28)-class) or Vipr2/VPAC2 genetic LOF titrated to abolish VPAC2-class neuroprotection/cognition attribution: residual VIP neuroprotective/cognitive phenotype remains ≥50% of the VIP without-VPAC2-abolish arm on the same panel. This is labeled an 'assumption-kill / vpac2-insufficiency' claim. Status: NEGATIVE (prediction, not yet tested). The matched residual-positive H2H experiment is EMPTY/UNKNOWN.

content_blocks.title: Scientific Rationale and Mechanism Sketch
content_blocks.content: VIP neuroprotection and cognition are framed as VPAC2-class attributed. P28 asks whether residual VIP neuroprotection/cognition under VPAC2 abolish still requires a path beyond VPAC2-class attribution (vpac2-insufficiency). Key mechanistic context: (1) Brenneman shows VIP neuronal survival under TTX electrical blockade — no Vipr2 LOF/PG 99-465 residual arm exists. (2) Gozes shows [St-Nle17]VIP Alzheimer-model culture NP and cholinergic-block spatial learning/memory phenotype — no VPAC2 residual arm. (3) Cunha-Reis shows PG 99-465 selective VPAC2 antagonist on VIP-enhanced CA1 transmission — both VPAC1 and VPAC2 contribute (VIP→VPAC1+VPAC2 honesty; not NP/cogn residual H2H). (4) Harmar shows Vipr2(-/-) circadian SCN LOF — circadian NON-MATCH for cogn/NP residual. (5) Rangon: VIP neonatal excitotoxic white-matter NP lost in Vipr2-lacking mice (VPAC2 agonists mimic; PACAP27/38 do not) — NECESSITY AGAINST residual. (6) Shoge: VIP6-28 antagonizes retinal VIP glutamate NP — NECESSITY AGAINST residual (VIP6-28 nonselective ≠ PG 99-465). (7) Zaben: VIP expands dentate precursors via VPAC2 or directs neuronal fate via VPAC1 — supports VIP→VPAC1 residual-path honesty under VPAC2-only abolish; not residual-positive H2H. (8) Ivanova soft: VIP+VIP(6-28) OBX cognition retain PAC1-attributed — not clean selective-VPAC2 residual.

content_blocks.title: Proposed Assay Design (Method: propose-assay)
content_blocks.content: Preferred experimental path: (1) Cell/slice/block-QC first — use PG 99-465 or Vipr2 ablation in Brenneman spinal-culture / Shoge retinal / Cunha-Reis hippocampal-slice style systems before new animal experiments. (2) In vivo panel remains primary kill path — Brenneman/Gozes-class or Rangon/Shoge-class matched rodent NP/cognition panel. (3) Design: ± VIP ± VPAC2 antagonist (PG 99-465 or VIP(6-28)-class) or Vipr2/VPAC2 genetic LOF; VPAC2-abolish condition must first abolish VPAC2-class NP/cognition attribution, then score residual VIP NP/cognition vs VIP without-VPAC2-abolish arm. (4) Include VPAC1-control arm for honesty. (5) Threshold: residual ≥50% of VIP without-VPAC2-abolish arm. (6) α/N pre-specified. Kill cost tier: 1; time to refute: 4 weeks; IP class: vpac2-insufficiency; vault hold: no.

content_blocks.title: Refutation Criteria and Actionable Limitations
content_blocks.content:
Refute if: On the pre-registered matched rodent NP/cognition panel ± VIP ± VPAC2 antagonist or Vipr2 LOF where VPAC2-abolish abolishes VPAC2-class attribution, residual VIP NP/cognitive phenotype is <50% of the VIP without-VPAC2-abolish arm — when abolish-fail, agonist-alone-null, underpowered strata, assay-mismatch, or nonselective-without-selective-confirmation artifacts are ruled out.

Key actionable limitations: (1) Do not treat P1–P27 as proving P28; Brenneman/Gozes phenotype, Cunha-Reis tool, Harmar circadian LOF, and Rangon/Shoge necessity priors are not a residual-under-VPAC2-abolish H2H. (2) Do not invent residual when EMPTY/UNKNOWN. (3) Do not treat necessity as residual-positive. (4) Do not invent dual-receptor residual. (5) Do not collapse VIP→VPAC1 honesty to PAC1/P26. (6) VIP≠PACAP; VPAC2≠PAC1 (critical). (7) VIP≠NPY; VPAC2≠Y1 (critical). (8) Abolish-fail/agonist-alone-null/underpowered/assay-mismatch leave test inconclusive rather than refuted.

key_findings: P28 hypothesis: residual VIP neuroprotective/cognitive phenotype ≥50% of VIP without-VPAC2-abolish arm persists under VPAC2 antagonist (PG 99-465 or VIP(6-28)-class) or Vipr2 LOF that abolishes VPAC2-class attribution — labeled assumption-kill/vpac2-insufficiency.
The matched residual-positive H2H experiment (VIP NP/cognition under VPAC2-abolish on Brenneman/Gozes-style panels) is EMPTY/UNKNOWN — no such experiment has been run.

Brenneman (PMID 3456568): VIP (0.1 nM most effective) prevents neuronal loss under TTX electrical blockade in spinal cord cultures; PHI-27/secretin inactive — survival phenotype PRIOR with no Vipr2 LOF/PG 99-465 residual arm.

Gozes (PMID 8552653): [St-Nle17]VIP prevents beta-amyloid culture neuron loss and cholinergic-block spatial learning/memory deficits (i.c.v./intranasal) — VIP-class Alzheimer NP/cognition phenotype PRIOR with no VPAC2 residual arm.

Cunha-Reis (PMID 15935995): PG 99-465 (VPAC2-selective) and PG 97-269 (VPAC1-selective) each inhibit VIP-enhanced CA1 synaptic transmission — confirms VIP→VPAC1+VPAC2 dual contribution; selective VPAC2 antagonist tool validated but not tested on NP/cognition endpoints.
Harmar (PMID 12086606): Vipr2(-/-) mice lose circadian SCN rest/activity and clock-gene rhythms — Vipr2 genetic LOF tool validated on circadian, NOT on cognition/neuroprotection residual.

Rangon (PMID 15872042, promoted): VIP neonatal excitotoxic white-matter NP is lost in Vipr2-lacking mice; VPAC2 agonists mimic; PACAP27/38 do not — NECESSITY AGAINST residual for neonatal WM NP panel; VIP≠PACAP.
Shoge (PMID 9795184, promoted): VIP6-28 antagonizes retinal VIP glutamate neuroprotection — NECESSITY AGAINST residual for retinal panel; VIP6-28 nonselective ≠ PG 99-465 VPAC2-selective.

Zaben (PMID 19650041, promoted): VIP expands dentate precursors via VPAC2 or directs neuronal fate via VPAC1 — supports VIP→VPAC1 residual-path honesty under VPAC2-only abolish; not residual-positive H2H.
Ivanova (PMID 22160165, adjacent): VIP+VIP(6-28) OBX cognition retain PAC1-attributed — not clean selective-VPAC2 residual; must not collapse to P26 (PACAP/PAC1).
Prior art shows NECESSITY AGAINST residual (Rangon, Shoge) but no matched residual-positive H2H under selective VPAC2 abolish on Brenneman/Gozes NP/cognition panels.

Proposed assay: cell/slice/block-QC first (PG 99-465 or Vipr2 ablation in Brenneman spinal-culture/Shoge retinal/Cunha-Reis hippocampal-slice style), then in vivo Brenneman/Gozes-class or Rangon/Shoge-class panel; include VPAC1-control arm; threshold ≥50% residual; kill cost tier 1; time to refute 4 weeks.
Execution status: NOT_RUN. FTO status: UNKNOWN. Status label: NEGATIVE.
